titulo: High in fibre, low in salt
intro: Reading a food label, talking about what is good or bad for you, and naming more of what is on the market stall.
b1.texto:
A label describes food with **rico en** and **bajo en**: **rico en** fibra, vitaminas, proteínas, hierro, calcio; **bajo en** calorías, sal, azúcar, grasas. And with **sin**: **sin** conservantes, **sin** colorantes, **sin** gluten.

**The state of food.** **Fresco**, **congelado**, **en conserva**. With **estar**: **está en buenas condiciones**, **está malo**, **está caducado**, **está podrido**. The date is **la fecha de caducidad**, and the yoghurt **caduca** mañana.

Remember the contrast: **es bueno** (it is good quality, or good for you) and **está bueno** (it tastes good).

**Groups.** **Las legumbres**: lentejas, garbanzos, judías. **Los frutos secos**: almendras, nueces, avellanas. **El marisco**: gambas, langostinos, mejillones, almejas. **El pescado azul** and **el pescado blanco**. **Las hierbas**: orégano, romero, tomillo, albahaca.

**Bread and flour.** **Harina de trigo**, **de maíz**; **pan integral**, **pan de molde**, **pan rallado**.

**Eating.** **Tener apetito**, **devorar**, **comer con moderación**, **hacer la digestión**, **digerir**, **ayunar**. A meal can be **ligera**, **pesada**, **abundante** or **escasa**; it can be **indigesta**.

**False friends.** **La nuez** is a walnut. **El conservante** is a preservative, and **el preservativo** is a condom.
b2.f0: The Mediterranean diet is not a weight-loss plan, but a traditional eating pattern in several regions.
b2.f1: It often includes vegetables, fruit, pulses, fish and olive oil, as well as moderate amounts of nuts.
b2.f2: Red meat and many highly processed products appear less often.
b2.f3: Some studies have associated this pattern with better cardiovascular health, although diet is only one factor that affects health.
b2.f4: Many families have less and less time to cook.
b2.f5: If this custom disappeared, recipes, ways of sharing food and knowledge about seasonal produce would disappear too.
b4.pregunta: According to the text, what is the Mediterranean diet?
b4.o0.refuerzo: Una forma de comer que se ha transmitido durante siglos.
b4.o1.refuerzo: No es un régimen para adelgazar.
b4.o2.refuerzo: It is much more than that.
b5.pregunta: According to the text, why do Spaniards follow it less?
b5.o0.refuerzo: Por falta de tiempo para cocinar.
b5.o1.refuerzo: Price is a distractor; the question asks why Spaniards follow the diet less.
b6.pregunta: Complete: this yoghurt is out of date.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Podrido is rotten, said of fruit or meat.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Legumbres means pulses, the dried seeds of beans, lentils and chickpeas.
b8.o0: a cereal high in fibre and low in sugar
b8.o1: a tasty cereal with fibre under the sugar
b8.o1.explicacion: Rico en: high in. Bajo en: low in.
b8.o2: an expensive cereal with little fibre
b10.traduccion: Pulses are rich in protein and iron.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write an article for a magazine on how eating habits have changed in your country.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Debate aloud: should governments tax sugary and processed food?
b8.o0.explicacion: Rico en fibra and bajo en azúcar mean high in fibre and low in sugar.
